v: The words of the Teacher,[^1] the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
דִּבְרֵי֙ קֹהֶ֣לֶת בֶּן־דָּוִ֔ד מֶ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
"Vapor of vapors,"[^2] says the Teacher, "vapor of vapors! Everything is vapor."
הֲבֵ֤ל הֲבָלִים֙ אָמַ֣ר קֹהֶ֔לֶת הֲבֵ֥ל הֲבָלִ֖ים הַכֹּ֥ל הָֽבֶל׃
What gain[^3] do people have from all their toil, all their toiling under the sun?[^4]
מַה־יִּתְר֖וֹן לָֽאָדָ֑ם בְּכָל־עֲמָל֔וֹ שֶֽׁיַּעֲמֹ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
A generation goes and a generation comes, but the earth stands forever.
דּ֤וֹר הֹלֵךְ֙ וְד֣וֹר בָּ֔א וְהָאָ֖רֶץ לְעוֹלָ֥ם עֹמָֽדֶת׃
The sun rises and the sun goes down, and it hurries, panting,[^5] back to its place, and there it rises again.
וְזָרַ֥ח הַשֶּׁ֖מֶשׁ וּבָ֣א הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֶ֨ל־מְקוֹמ֔וֹ שׁוֹאֵ֛ף זוֹרֵ֥חַֽ ה֖וּא שָֽׁם׃
It goes to the south and turns to the north; round and round goes the wind, and on its rounds the wind returns.
הוֹלֵךְ֙ אֶל־דָּר֔וֹם וְסוֹבֵ֖ב אֶל־צָפ֑וֹן סוֹבֵ֤ב ׀ סֹבֵב֙ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ הָר֔וּחַ וְעַל־סְבִיבֹתָ֖יו שָׁ֥ב הָרֽוּחַ׃
All the streams flow to the sea, yet the sea is never full. To the place where the streams flow, there they keep on flowing.[^6]
כָּל־הַנְּחָלִים֙ הֹלְכִ֣ים אֶל־הַיָּ֔ם וְהַיָּ֖ם אֵינֶ֣נּוּ מָלֵ֑א אֶל־מְק֗וֹם שֶׁ֤הַנְּחָלִים֙ הֹֽלְכִ֔ים שָׁ֛ם הֵ֥ם שָׁבִ֖ים לָלָֽכֶת׃
All things are weary,[^7] more than anyone can say. The eye is never satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים יְגֵעִ֔ים לֹא־יוּכַ֥ל אִ֖ישׁ לְדַבֵּ֑ר לֹא־תִשְׂבַּ֥ע עַ֙יִן֙ לִרְא֔וֹת וְלֹא־תִמָּלֵ֥א אֹ֖זֶן מִשְּׁמֹֽעַ׃
What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done. There is nothing new under the sun.
מַה־שֶּֽׁהָיָה֙ ה֣וּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֔ה וּמַה־שֶׁנַּֽעֲשָׂ֔ה ה֖וּא שֶׁיֵּעָשֶׂ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין כָּל־חָדָ֖שׁ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
There is a thing of which people say, "Look, this is new!" It was here already, in the ages before us.
יֵ֥שׁ דָּבָ֛ר שֶׁיֹּאמַ֥ר רְאֵה־זֶ֖ה חָדָ֣שׁ ה֑וּא כְּבָר֙ הָיָ֣ה לְעֹֽלָמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה מִלְּפָנֵֽנוּ׃
There is no remembrance of those who came before,[^8] and of those who are yet to come there will be no remembrance either, among those who come after them.
אֵ֥ין זִכְר֖וֹן לָרִאשֹׁנִ֑ים וְגַ֨ם לָאַחֲרֹנִ֜ים שֶׁיִּהְי֗וּ לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ זִכָּר֔וֹן עִ֥ם שֶׁיִּהְי֖וּ לָאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃ פ
I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
אֲנִ֣י קֹהֶ֗לֶת הָיִ֥יתִי מֶ֛לֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
I set my heart[^9] to seek and to explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven.[^10] It is an unhappy task[^11] that God has given human beings to keep them busy.[^12]
וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת־לִבִּ֗י לִדְר֤וֹשׁ וְלָתוּר֙ בַּֽחָכְמָ֔ה עַ֛ל כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם ה֣וּא ׀ עִנְיַ֣ן רָ֗ע נָתַ֧ן אֱלֹהִ֛ים לִבְנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם לַעֲנ֥וֹת בּֽוֹ׃
I have seen all the deeds that are done under the sun, and look, everything is vapor and chasing the wind.[^13]
רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַֽמַּעֲשִׂ֔ים שֶֽׁנַּעֲשׂ֖וּ תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכֹּ֛ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is missing cannot be counted.
מְעֻוָּ֖ת לֹא־יוּכַ֣ל לִתְקֹ֑ן וְחֶסְר֖וֹן לֹא־יוּכַ֥ל לְהִמָּנֽוֹת׃
I said to myself,[^14] "Look, I have grown great and gained more wisdom than all who ruled Jerusalem before me,[^15] and my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge."
דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי אֲנִ֤י עִם־לִבִּי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֲנִ֗י הִנֵּ֨ה הִגְדַּ֤לְתִּי וְהוֹסַ֙פְתִּי֙ חָכְמָ֔ה עַ֛ל כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה לְפָנַ֖י עַל־יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְלִבִּ֛י רָאָ֥ה הַרְבֵּ֖ה חָכְמָ֥ה וָדָֽעַת׃
So I set my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly. I learned that this too is chasing the wind.[^16]
וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת חָכְמָ֔ה וְדַ֥עַת הוֹלֵל֖וֹת וְשִׂכְל֑וּת יָדַ֕עְתִּי שֶׁגַּם־זֶ֥ה ה֖וּא רַעְי֥וֹן רֽוּחַ׃
For with much wisdom comes much grief, and whoever increases knowledge increases pain.
כִּ֛י בְּרֹ֥ב חָכְמָ֖ה רָב־כָּ֑עַס וְיוֹסִ֥יף דַּ֖עַת יוֹסִ֥יף מַכְאֽוֹב׃

n.1: Hebrew *Qohelet*, a title or pen name, from the verb *qahal*, "to gather, assemble": one who gathers or addresses an assembly, or perhaps one who gathers sayings (12:9). The Greek title of the book, *Ekklesiastes*, means a member or speaker of an assembly; the traditional English rendering is "the Preacher". The word is feminine in form, perhaps as the name of an office. It is "the Teacher" throughout (1:2, 12; 7:27; 12:8–10). The book does not name Solomon, though the description fits him.
n.2: Hebrew *havel havalim*. *Hevel* means "breath" or "vapor": something real but without substance, which cannot be grasped and soon vanishes. It is also Abel's name (Genesis 4:2). Ecclesiastes uses the word thirty-eight times for what is fleeting, futile, empty or beyond understanding. Traditionally it is translated "vanity", and in some modern versions "meaningless"; here it is "vapor" every time, so that readers can follow the pattern. "Vapor of vapors" is a superlative, like "Song of Songs": the merest vapor, utterly fleeting. The book ends with the same words (12:8).
n.3: Hebrew *yitron*, "gain, profit, what is left over", a word found only in Ecclesiastes. It is "gain" or "advantage" throughout.
n.4: "Under the sun" is the book's phrase for this world and human life in it, as people experience it. It occurs twenty-nine times, always translated the same way.
n.5: Hebrew *sho'ef*, "panting, gasping", or "hurrying": the sun is pictured as a weary runner.
n.6: Literally "there they return to go". Or "from there they go back again".
n.7: Or "All words are weary". Hebrew *devarim* means both "things" and "words".
n.8: Or "of the things that came before … of the things yet to come".
n.9: Literally "I gave my heart", that is, I applied my mind. In Hebrew the heart is the seat of thought and will. Also in verse 17.
n.10: Literally "under the heavens", a variation on "under the sun" (verse 3). Also in 2:3 and 3:1.
n.11: Hebrew *inyan ra*, "a bad business, an evil occupation".
n.12: Literally "to be busied with it". Or "to be afflicted with". *Inyan*, "task", and the verb here come from the same root.
n.13: Hebrew *re'ut ruach*, "pursuit of wind", or perhaps "shepherding the wind" (from *ra'ah*, "to tend, to herd"), something that can never be caught or held. Traditionally "vexation of spirit". The phrase occurs seven times, and a related form, *ra'yon ruach* (verse 17; 4:16), twice; both are "chasing the wind" throughout.
n.14: Literally "I spoke, I, with my heart".
n.15: Literally "all who were before me over Jerusalem".
n.16: Hebrew *ra'yon ruach*, a form of the phrase in verse 14.

v: I said to myself,[^1] "Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good."[^2] But look, this too was vapor.[^3]
אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י לְכָה־נָּ֛א אֲנַסְּכָ֛ה בְשִׂמְחָ֖ה וּרְאֵ֣ה בְט֑וֹב וְהִנֵּ֥ה גַם־ה֖וּא הָֽבֶל׃
Of laughter I said, "It is madness," and of pleasure, "What does it accomplish?"
לִשְׂח֖וֹק אָמַ֣רְתִּי מְהוֹלָ֑ל וּלְשִׂמְחָ֖ה מַה־זֹּ֥ה עֹשָֽׂה׃

I explored with my heart how to cheer my body with wine,[^4] while my heart still guided me with wisdom, and how to take hold of folly, until I could see what is good for human beings to do under heaven during the few days of their life.[^5]

תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י לִמְשׁ֥וֹךְ בַּיַּ֖יִן אֶת־בְּשָׂרִ֑י וְלִבִּ֞י נֹהֵ֤ג בַּֽחָכְמָה֙ וְלֶאֱחֹ֣ז בְּסִכְל֔וּת עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר־אֶרְאֶ֗ה אֵי־זֶ֨ה ט֜וֹב לִבְנֵ֤י הָאָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַעֲשׂוּ֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם מִסְפַּ֖ר יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּיהֶֽם׃
I did great things. I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.
הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י בָּנִ֤יתִי לִי֙ בָּתִּ֔ים נָטַ֥עְתִּי לִ֖י כְּרָמִֽים׃
I made myself gardens and parks,[^6] and I planted every kind of fruit tree in them.
עָשִׂ֣יתִי לִ֔י גַּנּ֖וֹת וּפַרְדֵּסִ֑ים וְנָטַ֥עְתִּי בָהֶ֖ם עֵ֥ץ כָּל־פֶּֽרִי׃
I made myself pools of water, to water from them a forest of growing trees.
עָשִׂ֥יתִי לִ֖י בְּרֵכ֣וֹת מָ֑יִם לְהַשְׁק֣וֹת מֵהֶ֔ם יַ֖עַר צוֹמֵ֥חַ עֵצִֽים׃
I bought male and female slaves, and I had slaves born in my house.[^7] I also had great herds and flocks, more than all who were in Jerusalem before me.
קָנִ֙יתִי֙ עֲבָדִ֣ים וּשְׁפָח֔וֹת וּבְנֵי־בַ֖יִת הָ֣יָה לִ֑י גַּ֣ם מִקְנֶה֩ בָקָ֨ר וָצֹ֤אן הַרְבֵּה֙ הָ֣יָה לִ֔י מִכֹּ֛ל שֶֽׁהָי֥וּ לְפָנַ֖י בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
I also gathered for myself silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I got myself male and female singers, and the delights of human beings: many concubines.[^8]
כָּנַ֤סְתִּי לִי֙ גַּם־כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב וּסְגֻלַּ֥ת מְלָכִ֖ים וְהַמְּדִינ֑וֹת עָשִׂ֨יתִי לִ֜י שָׁרִ֣ים וְשָׁר֗וֹת וְתַעֲנוּגֹ֛ת בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם שִׁדָּ֥ה וְשִׁדּֽוֹת׃
So I became great, greater than all who were in Jerusalem before me. My wisdom also stayed with me.
וְגָדַ֣לְתִּי וְהוֹסַ֔פְתִּי מִכֹּ֛ל שֶׁהָיָ֥ה לְפָנַ֖י בִּירוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם אַ֥ף חָכְמָתִ֖י עָ֥מְדָה לִּֽי׃
Whatever my eyes asked for, I did not keep from them. I did not hold back my heart from any pleasure, for my heart took pleasure in all my toil, and this was my portion[^9] from all my toil.
וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָֽׁאֲל֣וּ עֵינַ֔י לֹ֥א אָצַ֖לְתִּי מֵהֶ֑ם לֹֽא־מָנַ֨עְתִּי אֶת־לִבִּ֜י מִכָּל־שִׂמְחָ֗ה כִּֽי־לִבִּ֤י שָׂמֵ֙חַ֙ מִכָּל־עֲמָלִ֔י וְזֶֽה־הָיָ֥ה חֶלְקִ֖י מִכָּל־עֲמָלִֽי׃
Then I turned to look at all the works my hands had done, and at the toil I had toiled to do, and look, everything was vapor and chasing the wind.[^10] There was no gain under the sun.
וּפָנִ֣יתִֽי אֲנִ֗י בְּכָל־מַעֲשַׂי֙ שֶֽׁעָשׂ֣וּ יָדַ֔י וּבֶֽעָמָ֖ל שֶׁעָמַ֣לְתִּי לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת וְהִנֵּ֨ה הַכֹּ֥ל הֶ֙בֶל֙ וּרְע֣וּת ר֔וּחַ וְאֵ֥ין יִתְר֖וֹן תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
Then I turned to consider wisdom, and madness and folly. For what can the one do who comes after the king? Only what has already been done.[^11]
וּפָנִ֤יתִֽי אֲנִי֙ לִרְא֣וֹת חָכְמָ֔ה וְהוֹלֵל֖וֹת וְסִכְל֑וּת כִּ֣י ׀ מֶ֣ה הָאָדָ֗ם שֶׁיָּבוֹא֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־כְּבָ֖ר עָשֽׂוּהוּ׃
I saw that wisdom has an advantage[^12] over folly, as light has an advantage over darkness.
וְרָאִ֣יתִי אָ֔נִי שֶׁיֵּ֥שׁ יִתְר֛וֹן לַֽחָכְמָ֖ה מִן־הַסִּכְל֑וּת כִּֽיתְר֥וֹן הָא֖וֹר מִן־הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
The wise have eyes in their heads, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also knew that one fate[^13] befalls them all.
הֶֽחָכָם֙ עֵינָ֣יו בְּרֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְהַכְּסִ֖יל בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ הוֹלֵ֑ךְ וְיָדַ֣עְתִּי גַם־אָ֔נִי שֶׁמִּקְרֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד יִקְרֶ֥ה אֶת־כֻּלָּֽם׃
So I said to myself,[^14] "What befalls the fool will befall me too. Why then have I been so very wise?" And I said to myself that this too was vapor.
וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י כְּמִקְרֵ֤ה הַכְּסִיל֙ גַּם־אֲנִ֣י יִקְרֵ֔נִי וְלָ֧מָּה חָכַ֛מְתִּי אֲנִ֖י אָ֣ז יוֹתֵ֑ר וְדִבַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י שֶׁגַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃
For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, any more than of the fool, since in the days to come everything will already be forgotten. How the wise die, just like the fool!
כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין זִכְר֧וֹן לֶחָכָ֛ם עִֽם־הַכְּסִ֖יל לְעוֹלָ֑ם בְּשֶׁכְּבָ֞ר הַיָּמִ֤ים הַבָּאִים֙ הַכֹּ֣ל נִשְׁכָּ֔ח וְאֵ֛יךְ יָמ֥וּת הֶחָכָ֖ם עִֽם־הַכְּסִֽיל׃
So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me; for everything is vapor and chasing the wind.
וְשָׂנֵ֙אתִי֙ אֶת־הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים כִּ֣י רַ֤ע עָלַי֙ הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ כִּֽי־הַכֹּ֥ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
I hated all my toil at which I toil under the sun, because I must leave it to the one who will come after me.
וְשָׂנֵ֤אתִֽי אֲנִי֙ אֶת־כָּל־עֲמָלִ֔י שֶׁאֲנִ֥י עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ שֶׁ֣אַנִּיחֶ֔נּוּ לָאָדָ֖ם שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָֽי׃
And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he will be master of all my toil, all I toiled at and was wise in under the sun. This too is vapor.
וּמִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ הֶֽחָכָ֤ם יִהְיֶה֙ א֣וֹ סָכָ֔ל וְיִשְׁלַט֙ בְּכָל־עֲמָלִ֔י שֶֽׁעָמַ֥לְתִּי וְשֶׁחָכַ֖מְתִּי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ גַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃
So I turned and gave my heart up to despair over all the toil at which I had toiled under the sun.
וְסַבּ֥וֹתִֽי אֲנִ֖י לְיַאֵ֣שׁ אֶת־לִבִּ֑י עַ֚ל כָּל־הֶ֣עָמָ֔ל שֶׁעָמַ֖לְתִּי תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
For there is a person whose toil is done with wisdom, knowledge and skill, and he must give it as a portion to someone who did not toil for it. This too is vapor, and a great evil.
כִּי־יֵ֣שׁ אָדָ֗ם שֶׁעֲמָל֛וֹ בְּחָכְמָ֥ה וּבְדַ֖עַת וּבְכִשְׁר֑וֹן וּלְאָדָ֞ם שֶׁלֹּ֤א עָֽמַל־בּוֹ֙ יִתְּנֶ֣נּוּ חֶלְק֔וֹ גַּם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וְרָעָ֥ה רַבָּֽה׃
For what does a person get from all his toil and the striving of his heart[^15] at which he toils under the sun?
כִּ֠י מֶֽה־הֹוֶ֤ה לָֽאָדָם֙ בְּכָל־עֲמָל֔וֹ וּבְרַעְי֖וֹן לִבּ֑ו שְׁה֥וּא עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
For all his days are pain, and his task is grief; even at night his heart does not rest. This too is vapor.
כִּ֧י כָל־יָמָ֣יו מַכְאֹבִ֗ים וָכַ֙עַס֙ עִנְיָנ֔וֹ גַּם־בַּלַּ֖יְלָה לֹא־שָׁכַ֣ב לִבּ֑וֹ גַּם־זֶ֖ה הֶ֥בֶל הֽוּא׃
There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink and let himself enjoy his toil.[^16] This too, I saw, is from the hand of God.
אֵֽין־ט֤וֹב בָּאָדָם֙ שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְהֶרְאָ֧ה אֶת־נַפְשׁ֛וֹ ט֖וֹב בַּעֲמָל֑וֹ גַּם־זֹה֙ רָאִ֣יתִי אָ֔נִי כִּ֛י מִיַּ֥ד הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃
For who can eat, and who can find enjoyment,[^17] apart from me?[^18]
כִּ֣י מִ֥י יֹאכַ֛ל וּמִ֥י יָח֖וּשׁ ח֥וּץ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

For to the person who pleases him[^19] God gives wisdom, knowledge and joy, but to the sinner he gives the task of gathering and collecting, only to give it to the one who pleases God. This too is vapor and chasing the wind.
כִּ֤י לְאָדָם֙ שֶׁטּ֣וֹב לְפָנָ֔יו נָתַ֛ן חָכְמָ֥ה וְדַ֖עַת וְשִׂמְחָ֑ה וְלַחוֹטֶא֩ נָתַ֨ן עִנְיָ֜ן לֶאֱס֣וֹף וְלִכְנ֗וֹס לָתֵת֙ לְטוֹב֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים גַּם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃

n.1: Literally "I said, I, in my heart".
n.3: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor": what is fleeting, futile or beyond understanding; see 1:2.
n.4: Literally "how to draw my flesh with wine". The meaning of the verb is uncertain: perhaps "to cheer", "to stimulate" or "to indulge".
n.5: Literally "the number of the days of their life".
n.6: Hebrew *pardesim*, a Persian loanword for an enclosed park. It is the source of the English word "paradise".
n.8: Hebrew *shiddah ve-shiddot*, words found only here, of uncertain meaning. They are usually understood as "a concubine, and concubines" (perhaps from *shad*, "breast"); others take them as "a chest, and chests" of treasure. The singular and plural together express a great number.
n.9: Hebrew *cheleq*, "portion, share": what is allotted to someone. A key word in Ecclesiastes, always "portion".
n.11: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "For what the man who will come after the king, what they have already done". Or "For what is the man who comes after the king? He is the one whom they made king long ago."
n.12: Hebrew *yitron*, the word translated "gain" in verse 11; see 1:3.
n.13: Hebrew *miqreh*, "what happens, what befalls someone": here death.
n.14: Literally "in my heart". Also later in the verse.
n.15: Hebrew *ra'yon libbo*. *Ra'yon* is the word in "chasing the wind" (*ra'yon ruach*) in 1:17.
n.16: Literally "There is no good in a person that he should eat and drink and make his soul see good in his toil". Most take it to mean "nothing better than", as in 3:12, 22 and 8:15.
n.17: Hebrew *yachush*, a word of uncertain meaning: perhaps "enjoy", or "worry".
n.18: Or "more than I". The Septuagint reads "apart from him", that is, apart from God.
n.19: Literally "who is good before him". Also later in the verse.

v: For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter[^1] under heaven:[^2]
לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת לְכָל־חֵ֖פֶץ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ ס
a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted;
עֵ֥ת לָלֶ֖דֶת וְעֵ֣ת לָמ֑וּת עֵ֣ת לָטַ֔עַת וְעֵ֖ת לַעֲק֥וֹר נָטֽוּעַ׃
a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build up;
עֵ֤ת לַהֲרוֹג֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִרְפּ֔וֹא עֵ֥ת לִפְר֖וֹץ וְעֵ֥ת לִבְנֽוֹת׃
a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance;
עֵ֤ת לִבְכּוֹת֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂח֔וֹק עֵ֥ת סְפ֖וֹד וְעֵ֥ת רְקֽוֹד׃
a time to throw stones away and a time to gather stones,[^3] a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing;
עֵ֚ת לְהַשְׁלִ֣יךְ אֲבָנִ֔ים וְעֵ֖ת כְּנ֣וֹס אֲבָנִ֑ים עֵ֣ת לַחֲב֔וֹק וְעֵ֖ת לִרְחֹ֥ק מֵחַבֵּֽק׃
a time to seek and a time to lose, a time to keep and a time to throw away;
עֵ֤ת לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ וְעֵ֣ת לְאַבֵּ֔ד עֵ֥ת לִשְׁמ֖וֹר וְעֵ֥ת לְהַשְׁלִֽיךְ׃
a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to be silent and a time to speak;
עֵ֤ת לִקְר֙וֹעַ֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִתְפּ֔וֹר עֵ֥ת לַחֲשׁ֖וֹת וְעֵ֥ת לְדַבֵּֽר׃
a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
עֵ֤ת לֶֽאֱהֹב֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂנֹ֔א עֵ֥ת מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְעֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם׃ ס
What gain[^4] does the worker have from his toil?
מַה־יִּתְרוֹן֙ הָֽעוֹשֶׂ֔ה בַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר ה֥וּא עָמֵֽל׃
I have seen the task that God has given human beings to keep them busy.
רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־הָֽעִנְיָ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן אֱלֹהִ֛ים לִבְנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם לַעֲנ֥וֹת בּֽוֹ׃
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity[^5] in their hearts, yet so that[^6] no one can find out the work that God has done from beginning to end.
אֶת־הַכֹּ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה יָפֶ֣ה בְעִתּ֑וֹ גַּ֤ם אֶת־הָעֹלָם֙ נָתַ֣ן בְּלִבָּ֔ם מִבְּלִ֞י אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹא־יִמְצָ֣א הָאָדָ֗ם אֶת־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים מֵרֹ֥אשׁ וְעַד־סֽוֹף׃
I know that there is nothing better for them than to be glad and to do good[^7] while they live.
יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין ט֖וֹב בָּ֑ם כִּ֣י אִם־לִשְׂמ֔וֹחַ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת ט֖וֹב בְּחַיָּֽיו׃
And also, when anyone eats and drinks and enjoys[^8] all his toil, that is the gift of God.
וְגַ֤ם כָּל־הָאָדָם֙ שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְרָאָ֥ה ט֖וֹב בְּכָל־עֲמָל֑וֹ מַתַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃
I know that whatever God does will last forever. Nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it. God has done it so that people will fear him.[^9]
יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּ֠י כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה הָאֱלֹהִים֙ ה֚וּא יִהְיֶ֣ה לְעוֹלָ֔ם עָלָיו֙ אֵ֣ין לְהוֹסִ֔יף וּמִמֶּ֖נּוּ אֵ֣ין לִגְרֹ֑עַ וְהָאֱלֹהִ֣ים עָשָׂ֔ה שֶׁיִּֽרְא֖וּ מִלְּפָנָֽיו׃
What has been is already here, and what is to be has already been, and God seeks out what has passed by.[^10]
מַה־שֶּֽׁהָיָה֙ כְּבָ֣ר ה֔וּא וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לִהְי֖וֹת כְּבָ֣ר הָיָ֑ה וְהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־נִרְדָּֽף׃
And I saw something else under the sun: in the place of justice, there was wickedness, and in the place of righteousness, there was wickedness.
וְע֥וֹד רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ מְק֤וֹם הַמִּשְׁפָּט֙ שָׁ֣מָּה הָרֶ֔שַׁע וּמְק֥וֹם הַצֶּ֖דֶק שָׁ֥מָּה הָרָֽשַׁע׃
I said to myself,[^11] "God will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every matter and for every deed there."[^12]
אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י אֶת־הַצַּדִּיק֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣רָשָׁ֔ע יִשְׁפֹּ֖ט הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּי־עֵ֣ת לְכָל־חֵ֔פֶץ וְעַ֥ל כָּל־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שָֽׁם׃
I said to myself about human beings, "God is testing them,[^13] to show them that they are animals, nothing more."[^14]
אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י עַל־דִּבְרַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם לְבָרָ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְלִרְא֕וֹת שְׁהֶם־בְּהֵמָ֥ה הֵ֖מָּה לָהֶֽם׃

For the fate[^15] of human beings and the fate of animals is one and the same: as one dies, so dies the other. They all have the same breath,[^16] and humans have no advantage over animals, for everything is vapor.[^17]
כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי־הָאָדָ֜ם וּמִקְרֶ֣ה הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וּמִקְרֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ לָהֶ֔ם כְּמ֥וֹת זֶה֙ כֵּ֣ן מ֣וֹת זֶ֔ה וְר֥וּחַ אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל וּמוֹתַ֨ר הָאָדָ֤ם מִן־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ אָ֔יִן כִּ֥י הַכֹּ֖ל הָֽבֶל׃
All go to one place. All came from the dust, and all return to the dust.
הַכֹּ֥ל הוֹלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד הַכֹּל֙ הָיָ֣ה מִן־הֶֽעָפָ֔ר וְהַכֹּ֖ל שָׁ֥ב אֶל־הֶעָפָֽר׃
Who knows whether the spirit of human beings goes upward, and whether the spirit of animals goes down into the earth?[^18]
מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ ר֚וּחַ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם הָעֹלָ֥ה הִ֖יא לְמָ֑עְלָה וְר֙וּחַ֙ הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה הַיֹּרֶ֥דֶת הִ֖יא לְמַ֥טָּה לָאָֽרֶץ׃
So I saw that there is nothing better than for people to rejoice in their works, for that is their portion. For who can bring them to see what will happen after them?
וְרָאִ֗יתִי כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין טוֹב֙ מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׂמַ֤ח הָאָדָם֙ בְּֽמַעֲשָׂ֔יו כִּי־ה֖וּא חֶלְק֑וֹ כִּ֣י מִ֤י יְבִיאֶ֙נּוּ֙ לִרְא֔וֹת בְּמֶ֖ה שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָֽיו׃

n.1: Hebrew *chefets*, "delight, desire", and in later Hebrew "matter, affair". Also in verse 17.
n.3: The meaning of the stones is uncertain: perhaps clearing a field and gathering stones for building, or ruining an enemy's field with stones (2 Kings 3:19, 25).
n.5: Hebrew *ha-olam*, "eternity", the distant past and future. Others suggest "a sense of the ages", "the world", or, from a root meaning "to hide", "darkness, ignorance".
n.7: Or "to enjoy themselves". Literally "to do good in his life".
n.10: Literally "God seeks what is pursued". The sense may be that God brings back what has gone by, or that God looks after those who are pursued.
n.11: Literally "I said, I, in my heart". Also in verse 18.
n.12: The sense of "there" is uncertain: perhaps with God, or at the judgment.
n.14: Literally "that they are animals, they themselves".
n.16: Hebrew *ruach*, "breath, spirit, wind". Also in verse 21, where it is "spirit".
n.18: Or "Who knows the spirit of human beings, which goes upward, and the spirit of animals, which goes down into the earth?" The Hebrew vowel points read it this way. The same consonants can be read as questions, as followed here and in the Septuagint.

v: Again I saw all the oppression that is done under the sun. Look, the tears of the oppressed, and they have no one to comfort them! Power is on the side of their oppressors,[^1] and they have no one to comfort them.

וְשַׁ֣בְתִּֽי אֲנִ֗י וָאֶרְאֶה֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָ֣עֲשֻׁקִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשִׂ֖ים תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ דִּמְעַ֣ת הָעֲשֻׁקִ֗ים וְאֵ֤ין לָהֶם֙ מְנַחֵ֔ם וּמִיַּ֤ד עֹֽשְׁקֵיהֶם֙ כֹּ֔חַ וְאֵ֥ין לָהֶ֖ם מְנַחֵֽם׃
So I praised the dead, who have already died, more than the living, who are still alive.
וְשַׁבֵּ֧חַ אֲנִ֛י אֶת־הַמֵּתִ֖ים שֶׁכְּבָ֣ר מֵ֑תוּ מִן־הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥מָּה חַיִּ֖ים עֲדֶֽנָה׃
But better than both is the one who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
וְטוֹב֙ מִשְּׁנֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־עֲדֶ֖ן לֹ֣א הָיָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־רָאָה֙ אֶת־הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה הָרָ֔ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
I saw that all toil and all skill in work comes from one person's envy of another.[^2] This too is vapor[^3] and chasing the wind.[^4]
וְרָאִ֨יתִֽי אֲנִ֜י אֶת־כָּל־עָמָ֗ל וְאֵת֙ כָּל־כִּשְׁר֣וֹן הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה כִּ֛י הִ֥יא קִנְאַת־אִ֖ישׁ מֵרֵעֵ֑הוּ גַּם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
The fool folds his hands and eats his own flesh.[^5]
הַכְּסִיל֙ חֹבֵ֣ק אֶת־יָדָ֔יו וְאֹכֵ֖ל אֶת־בְּשָׂרֽוֹ׃
Better one handful with rest than two fistfuls with toil and chasing the wind.
ט֕וֹב מְלֹ֥א כַ֖ף נָ֑חַת מִמְּלֹ֥א חָפְנַ֛יִם עָמָ֖ל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
Again I saw vapor under the sun:
וְשַׁ֧בְתִּי אֲנִ֛י וָאֶרְאֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

There is someone who is alone, without a second;[^6] he has neither son nor brother. Yet there is no end to all his toil, and his eye[^7] is never satisfied with riches. "For whom am I toiling, and depriving myself of good things?"[^8] This too is vapor and an unhappy task.

יֵ֣שׁ אֶחָד֩ וְאֵ֨ין שֵׁנִ֜י גַּ֣ם בֵּ֧ן וָאָ֣ח אֵֽין־ל֗וֹ וְאֵ֥ין קֵץ֙ לְכָל־עֲמָל֔וֹ גַּם־*עיניו **עֵינ֖וֹ לֹא־תִשְׂבַּ֣ע עֹ֑שֶׁר וּלְמִ֣י ׀ אֲנִ֣י עָמֵ֗ל וּמְחַסֵּ֤ר אֶת־נַפְשִׁי֙ מִטּוֹבָ֔ה גַּם־זֶ֥[t]ה הֶ֛בֶל וְעִנְיַ֥ן רָ֖ע הֽוּא׃
Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil.
טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן־הָאֶחָ֑ד אֲשֶׁ֧ר יֵשׁ־לָהֶ֛ם שָׂכָ֥ר ט֖וֹב בַּעֲמָלָֽם׃
For if they fall, one will lift up his companion. But pity the one who falls alone,[^9] with no second to lift him up!
כִּ֣י אִם־יִפֹּ֔לוּ הָאֶחָ֖ד יָקִ֣ים אֶת־חֲבֵר֑וֹ וְאִ֣יל֗וֹ הָֽאֶחָד֙ שֶׁיִפּ֔וֹל וְאֵ֥ין שֵׁנִ֖י לַהֲקִימֽוֹ׃
Again, if two lie down together, they keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?
גַּ֛ם אִם־יִשְׁכְּב֥וּ שְׁנַ֖יִם וְחַ֣ם לָהֶ֑ם וּלְאֶחָ֖ד אֵ֥יךְ יֵחָֽם׃
And if someone overpowers one who is alone, two can stand against him.[^10] A three-stranded cord is not quickly broken.
וְאִֽם־יִתְקְפוֹ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם יַעַמְד֣וּ נֶגְדּ֑וֹ וְהַחוּט֙ הַֽמְשֻׁלָּ֔שׁ לֹ֥א בִמְהֵרָ֖ה יִנָּתֵֽק׃
Better a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take advice.
ט֛וֹב יֶ֥לֶד מִסְכֵּ֖ן וְחָכָ֑ם מִמֶּ֤לֶךְ זָקֵן֙ וּכְסִ֔יל אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־יָדַ֥ע לְהִזָּהֵ֖ר עֽוֹד׃
For he came out of prison[^11] to become king, though he was born poor in his kingdom.[^12]
כִּֽי־מִבֵּ֥ית הָסוּרִ֖ים יָצָ֣א לִמְלֹ֑ךְ כִּ֛י גַּ֥ם בְּמַלְכוּת֖וֹ נוֹלַ֥ד רָֽשׁ׃
I saw all the living who walk under the sun following[^13] the youth, the second one,[^14] who would stand in his place.
רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים הַֽמְהַלְּכִ֖ים תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עִ֚ם הַיֶּ֣לֶד הַשֵּׁנִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
There was no end to all the people, to all whom he led,[^15] yet those who come later will not rejoice in him. This too is vapor and chasing the wind.[^16]
אֵֽין־קֵ֣ץ לְכָל־הָעָ֗ם לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־הָיָה֙ לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם גַּ֥ם הָאַחֲרוֹנִ֖ים לֹ֣א יִשְׂמְחוּ־ב֑וֹ כִּֽי־גַם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וְרַעְי֥וֹן רֽוּחַ׃
Guard your steps[^17] when you go to the house of God. To draw near to listen[^18] is better than for fools to offer a sacrifice, for they do not know that they are doing evil.[^19]
שְׁמֹ֣ר *רגליך **רַגְלְךָ֗ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר תֵּלֵךְ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְקָר֣וֹב לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ מִתֵּ֥ת הַכְּסִילִ֖ים זָ֑בַח כִּֽי־אֵינָ֥ם יוֹדְעִ֖ים לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת רָֽע׃

n.1: Literally "and from the hand of their oppressors, power".
n.2: Literally "that it is the envy of a man from his neighbor". Or "the rivalry between one person and another".
n.5: That is, he ruins himself through idleness.
n.6: Literally "There is one, and there is no second".
n.7: The Hebrew text is written "his eyes" but read "his eye".
n.8: The Hebrew moves into the first person without saying who is speaking.
n.9: Literally "But woe to him, the one who falls".
n.10: Literally "And if someone overpowers him, the one, the two will stand against him".
n.12: The Hebrew does not make clear who "he" is in each part of this verse. It may be the youth, who rose from prison to the throne though born poor; "in his kingdom" may mean in the old king's kingdom. Or it may be the king, who came out of prison to reign, while the poor youth was born in his kingdom.
n.14: Perhaps the youth of verse 13, who succeeds the old king, or another youth who takes his place in turn.
n.15: Literally "to all before whom he was". Or "to all who were before them", that is, earlier generations.
n.17: Literally "Guard your foot". The Hebrew text is written "your feet" but read "your foot". Verse 17 is 5:1 in most English Bibles.
n.18: To listen often means to obey.
n.19: Literally "for they do not know to do evil".

v: Do not be quick with your mouth, and do not let your heart hurry to bring out a word before God.[^1] For God is in heaven and you are on earth, so let your words be few.
אַל־תְּבַהֵ֨ל עַל־פִּ֜יךָ וְלִבְּךָ֧ אַל־יְמַהֵ֛ר לְהוֹצִ֥יא דָבָ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים בַּשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְאַתָּ֣ה עַל־הָאָ֔רֶץ עַֽ[t]ל־כֵּ֛ן יִהְי֥וּ דְבָרֶ֖יךָ מְעַטִּֽים׃
For a dream comes with much busyness,[^2] and the voice of a fool with many words.
כִּ֛י בָּ֥א הַחֲל֖וֹם בְּרֹ֣ב עִנְיָ֑ן וְק֥וֹל כְּסִ֖יל בְּרֹ֥ב דְּבָרִֽים׃
When you make a vow to God, do not delay to fulfill it, for he has no pleasure in fools. Fulfill what you vow.[^3]
כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ תִּדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר לֽ͏ֵאלֹהִ֗ים אַל־תְּאַחֵר֙ לְשַׁלְּמ֔וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין חֵ֖פֶץ בַּכְּסִילִ֑ים אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־תִּדֹּ֖ר שַׁלֵּֽם׃
It is better not to vow than to vow and not fulfill it.
ט֖וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־תִדֹּ֑ר מִשֶׁתִּדּ֖וֹר וְלֹ֥א תְשַׁלֵּֽם׃
Do not let your mouth make your flesh[^4] sin, and do not say before the messenger[^5] that it was a mistake.[^6] Why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?
אַל־תִּתֵּ֤ן אֶת־פִּ֙יךָ֙ לַחֲטִ֣יא אֶת־בְּשָׂרֶ֔ךָ וְאַל־תֹּאמַר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמַּלְאָ֔ךְ כִּ֥י שְׁגָגָ֖ה הִ֑יא לָ֣מָּה יִקְצֹ֤ף הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ עַל־קוֹלֶ֔ךָ וְחִבֵּ֖ל אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדֶֽיךָ׃
For when dreams are many, so are vapors[^7] and words.[^8] But fear God.
כִּ֣י בְרֹ֤ב חֲלֹמוֹת֙ וַהֲבָלִ֔ים וּדְבָרִ֖ים הַרְבֵּ֑ה כִּ֥י אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְרָֽא׃

If you see the poor oppressed, and justice and righteousness robbed in the province, do not be amazed at the matter, for one high official is watched by a higher one, and there are higher ones over them.[^9]
אִם־עֹ֣שֶׁק רָ֠שׁ וְגֵ֨זֶל מִשְׁפָּ֤ט וָצֶ֙דֶק֙ תִּרְאֶ֣ה בַמְּדִינָ֔ה אַל־תִּתְמַ֖הּ עַל־הַחֵ֑פֶץ כִּ֣י גָבֹ֜הַּ מֵעַ֤ל גָּבֹ֙הַ֙ שֹׁמֵ֔ר וּגְבֹהִ֖ים עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
But the gain[^10] of a land in every way is this: a king for the cultivated field.[^11]
וְיִתְר֥וֹן אֶ֖רֶץ בַּכֹּ֣ל *היא **ה֑וּא מֶ֥לֶךְ לְשָׂדֶ֖ה נֶעֱבָֽד׃
Whoever loves money[^12] will never be satisfied with money, and whoever loves wealth will never be satisfied with income. This too is vapor.
אֹהֵ֥ב כֶּ֙סֶף֙ לֹא־יִשְׂבַּ֣ע כֶּ֔סֶף וּמִֽי־אֹהֵ֥ב בֶּהָמ֖וֹן לֹ֣א תְבוּאָ֑ה גַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃
When good things increase, those who eat them increase. And what advantage is there to their owner, except to see them with his eyes?
בִּרְבוֹת֙ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה רַבּ֖וּ אוֹכְלֶ֑יהָ וּמַה־כִּשְׁרוֹן֙ לִבְעָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֖י אִם־*ראית **רְא֥וּת עֵינָֽיו׃
Sweet is the sleep of the laborer, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich[^13] will not let him sleep.
מְתוּקָה֙ שְׁנַ֣ת הָעֹבֵ֔ד אִם־מְעַ֥ט וְאִם־הַרְבֵּ֖ה יֹאכֵ֑ל וְהַשָּׂבָע֙ לֶֽעָשִׁ֔יר אֵינֶ֛נּוּ מַנִּ֥יחַֽ ל֖וֹ לִישֽׁוֹן׃
There is a grievous evil[^14] I have seen under the sun: riches kept by their owner to his harm.
יֵ֚שׁ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עֹ֛שֶׁר שָׁמ֥וּר לִבְעָלָ֖יו לְרָעָתֽוֹ׃
Those riches are lost in some bad venture,[^15] and he has fathered a son, but there is nothing in his hand.
וְאָבַ֛ד הָעֹ֥שֶׁר הַה֖וּא בְּעִנְיַ֣ן רָ֑ע וְהוֹלִ֣יד בֵּ֔ן וְאֵ֥ין בְּיָד֖וֹ מְאֽוּמָה׃
As he came from his mother's womb, so he will go again, naked as he came.[^16] He will take nothing for his toil that he can carry in his hand.
כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר יָצָא֙ מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמּ֔וֹ עָר֛וֹם יָשׁ֥וּב לָלֶ֖כֶת כְּשֶׁבָּ֑א וּמְא֙וּמָה֙ לֹא־יִשָּׂ֣א בַעֲמָל֔וֹ שֶׁיֹּלֵ֖ךְ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
This too is a grievous evil: exactly as he came, so he will go. And what gain does he have, who toils for the wind?
וְגַם־זֹה֙ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה כָּל־עֻמַּ֥ת שֶׁבָּ֖א כֵּ֣ן יֵלֵ֑ךְ וּמַה־יִּתְר֣וֹן ל֔וֹ שֶֽׁיַּעֲמֹ֖ל לָרֽוּחַ׃
All his days, too, he eats in darkness, with much grief, sickness and anger.[^17]
גַּ֥ם כָּל־יָמָ֖יו בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יֹאכֵ֑ל וְכָעַ֥ס הַרְבֵּ֖ה וְחָלְי֥וֹ וָקָֽצֶף׃

Look, this is what I have seen to be good and fitting:[^18] to eat and drink and enjoy[^19] all the toil at which one toils under the sun during the few days of life[^20] that God has given him, for this is his portion.

הִנֵּ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־רָאִ֣יתִי אָ֗נִי ט֣וֹב אֲשֶׁר־יָפֶ֣ה לֶֽאֶכוֹל־וְ֠לִשְׁתּוֹת וְלִרְא֨וֹת טוֹבָ֜ה בְּכָל־עֲמָל֣וֹ ׀ שֶׁיַּעֲמֹ֣ל תַּֽחַת־הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ מִסְפַּ֧ר יְמֵי־*חיו **חַיָּ֛יו אֲשֶׁר־נָֽתַן־ל֥וֹ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים כִּי־ה֥וּא חֶלְקֽוֹ׃
Also, whenever God gives anyone riches and possessions, and enables him to eat from them, to accept his portion and to rejoice in his toil, this is the gift of God.
גַּ֣ם כָּֽל־הָאָדָ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן־ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִים֩ עֹ֨שֶׁר וּנְכָסִ֜ים וְהִשְׁלִיט֨וֹ לֶאֱכֹ֤ל מִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ וְלָשֵׂ֣את אֶת־חֶלְק֔וֹ וְלִשְׂמֹ֖חַ בַּעֲמָל֑וֹ זֹ֕ה מַתַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃
For he will not dwell much on the days of his life,[^21] because God keeps him busy[^22] with the joy of his heart.
כִּ֚י לֹ֣א הַרְבֵּ֔ה יִזְכֹּ֖ר אֶת־יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֑יו כִּ֧י הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים מַעֲנֶ֖ה בְּשִׂמְחַ֥ת לִבּֽוֹ׃

n.3: Compare Deuteronomy 23:22–24 (23:21–23 in most English Bibles).
n.5: Hebrew *mal'akh*, "messenger", perhaps a priest or temple official (compare Malachi 2:7). The Septuagint reads "before God".
n.6: Hebrew *shegagah*, the word used for an unintentional sin in Leviticus 4 and Numbers 15.

n.9: Literally "for a high one watches over a high one, and high ones are over them". This may mean that officials protect one another, or that each is watched by another above him.
n.11: The Hebrew is obscure. Literally "And the gain of a land in all, it is, a king for a field that is worked". Perhaps "a king who cares for the farmland", or "even a king is served by the field".
n.12: Literally "silver". Also later in the verse.
n.13: Or "the full stomach of the rich".
n.14: Literally "a sick evil". Also in verse 15.
n.15: Hebrew *inyan ra*, the phrase translated "an unhappy task" in 1:13 and 4:8.
n.17: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "and he has much grief, and his sickness, and wrath".
n.18: Literally "what I have seen, I: good that is beautiful".
n.20: Literally "the number of the days of his life".
n.21: Or "For he will hardly notice the days of his life passing". Literally "For he will not much remember the days of his life".

v: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, and it lies heavy on human beings:[^1]
יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וְרַבָּ֥ה הִ֖יא עַל־הָאָדָֽם׃

a man to whom God gives riches, possessions and honor, so that he lacks nothing he desires, yet God does not give him the power to eat from them, but a stranger eats them. This is vapor[^2] and a grievous sickness.[^3]

אִ֣ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתֶּן־ל֣וֹ הָאֱלֹהִ֡ים עֹשֶׁר֩ וּנְכָסִ֨ים וְכָב֜וֹד וְֽאֵינֶ֨נּוּ חָסֵ֥ר לְנַפְשׁ֣וֹ ׀ מִכֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־יִתְאַוֶּ֗ה וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁלִיטֶ֤נּוּ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל מִמֶּ֔נּוּ כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ נָכְרִ֖י יֹֽאכֲלֶ֑נּוּ זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וָחֳלִ֥י רָ֖ע הֽוּא׃

If a man fathers a hundred children[^4] and lives many years, however many the days of his years may be, if he is not satisfied with good things,[^5] and he has no burial either,[^6] I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

אִם־יוֹלִ֣יד אִ֣ישׁ מֵאָ֡ה וְשָׁנִים֩ רַבּ֨וֹת יִֽחְיֶ֜ה וְרַ֣ב ׀ שֶׁיִּהְי֣וּ יְמֵֽי־שָׁנָ֗יו וְנַפְשׁוֹ֙ לֹא־תִשְׂבַּ֣ע מִן־הַטּוֹבָ֔ה וְגַם־קְבוּרָ֖ה לֹא־הָ֣יְתָה לּ֑וֹ אָמַ֕רְתִּי ט֥וֹב מִמֶּ֖נּוּ הַנָּֽפֶל׃
For it comes in vapor and goes in darkness, and in darkness its name is covered.
כִּֽי־בַהֶ֥בֶל בָּ֖א וּבַחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יֵלֵ֑ךְ וּבַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ שְׁמ֥וֹ יְכֻסֶּֽה׃
It has not even seen the sun or known anything, yet it has more rest than he.
גַּם־שֶׁ֥מֶשׁ לֹא־רָאָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע נַ֥חַת לָזֶ֖ה מִזֶּֽה׃
Even if he lived a thousand years twice over, but did not enjoy[^7] good things, do not all go to one place?
וְאִלּ֣וּ חָיָ֗ה אֶ֤לֶף שָׁנִים֙ פַּעֲמַ֔יִם וְטוֹבָ֖ה לֹ֣א רָאָ֑ה הֲלֹ֛א אֶל־מָק֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד הַכֹּ֥ל הוֹלֵֽךְ׃
All the toil of human beings is for their mouth, yet the appetite[^8] is never filled.
כָּל־עֲמַ֥ל הָאָדָ֖ם לְפִ֑יהוּ וְגַם־הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ לֹ֥א תִמָּלֵֽא׃
For what advantage does the wise have over the fool? What does the poor person gain by knowing how to conduct himself before the living?[^9]
כִּ֛י מַה־יוֹתֵ֥ר לֶחָכָ֖ם מִֽן־הַכְּסִ֑יל מַה־לֶּעָנִ֣י יוֹדֵ֔עַ לַהֲלֹ֖ךְ נֶ֥גֶד הַחַיִֽים׃
Better is what the eyes see than the wandering of desire.[^10] This too is vapor and chasing the wind.[^11]
ט֛וֹב מַרְאֵ֥ה עֵינַ֖יִם מֵֽהֲלָךְ־נָ֑פֶשׁ גַּם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
Whatever exists has already been named, and it is known what a human being is:[^12] he cannot contend with one who is stronger than he.[^13]
מַה־שֶּֽׁהָיָ֗ה כְּבָר֙ נִקְרָ֣א שְׁמ֔וֹ וְנוֹדָ֖ע אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא אָדָ֑ם וְלֹא־יוּכַ֣ל לָדִ֔ין עִ֥ם *שהתקיף **שֶׁתַּקִּ֖יף מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃
The more words, the more vapor;[^14] and what advantage is that to anyone?
כִּ֛י יֵשׁ־דְּבָרִ֥ים הַרְבֵּ֖ה מַרְבִּ֣ים הָ֑בֶל מַה־יֹּתֵ֖ר לָאָדָֽם׃
For who knows what is good for a person in life, during the few days of his life of vapor,[^15] which he passes like a shadow? For who can tell anyone what will happen after him under the sun?
כִּ֣י מִֽי־יוֹדֵעַ֩ מַה־טּ֨וֹב לָֽאָדָ֜ם בַּֽחַיִּ֗ים מִסְפַּ֛ר יְמֵי־חַיֵּ֥י הֶבְל֖וֹ וְיַעֲשֵׂ֣ם כַּצֵּ֑ל אֲשֶׁר֙ מִֽי־יַגִּ֣יד לָֽאָדָ֔ם מַה־יִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָ֖יו תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

n.1: Or "and it is common among human beings".
n.5: Literally "if his soul is not satisfied with good".
n.6: To lack a proper burial was a great disgrace.
n.9: Literally "What to the poor man who knows how to walk before the living?"
n.10: Literally "than the going of the *nephesh*", the appetite that roams after what it does not have.
n.12: Or "and it is known that he is human (*adam*)", perhaps recalling that the first human was named from the ground, *adamah* (Genesis 2:7).
n.14: Literally "For there are many words that increase vapor".
n.15: Literally "the number of the days of the life of his vapor".

v: A good name is better than good oil,[^1] and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
ט֥וֹב שֵׁ֖ם מִשֶּׁ֣מֶן ט֑וֹב וְי֣וֹם הַמָּ֔וֶת מִיּ֖וֹם הִוָּלְדֽוֹ׃
It is better to go to a house of mourning than to go to a house of feasting, for that is the end of every person, and the living will take it to heart.
ט֞וֹב לָלֶ֣כֶת אֶל־בֵּֽית־אֵ֗בֶל מִלֶּ֙כֶת֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה בַּאֲשֶׁ֕ר ה֖וּא ס֣וֹף כָּל־הָאָדָ֑ם וְהַחַ֖י יִתֵּ֥ן אֶל־לִבּֽוֹ׃
Grief[^2] is better than laughter, for when the face is sad the heart may be glad.[^3]
ט֥וֹב כַּ֖עַס מִשְּׂחֹ֑ק כִּֽי־בְרֹ֥עַ פָּנִ֖ים יִ֥יטַב לֵֽב׃
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
לֵ֤ב חֲכָמִים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִילִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית שִׂמְחָֽה׃
It is better to listen to the rebuke of the wise than to listen to the song of fools.
ט֕וֹב לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ גַּעֲרַ֣ת חָכָ֑ם מֵאִ֕ישׁ שֹׁמֵ֖עַ שִׁ֥יר כְּסִילִֽים׃
For like the crackling of thorns under a pot,[^4] so is the laughter of the fool. This too is vapor.[^5]
כִּ֣י כְק֤וֹל הַסִּירִים֙ תַּ֣חַת הַסִּ֔יר כֵּ֖ן שְׂחֹ֣ק הַכְּסִ֑יל וְגַם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃
Surely oppression[^6] makes the wise foolish, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
כִּ֥י הָעֹ֖שֶׁק יְהוֹלֵ֣ל חָכָ֑ם וִֽיאַבֵּ֥ד אֶת־לֵ֖ב מַתָּנָֽה׃
Better is the end of a thing than its beginning; better a patient spirit than a proud spirit.[^7]
ט֛וֹב אַחֲרִ֥ית דָּבָ֖ר מֽ͏ֵרֵאשִׁית֑וֹ ט֥וֹב אֶֽרֶךְ־ר֖וּחַ מִגְּבַהּ־רֽוּחַ׃
Do not be quick in your spirit to become angry,[^8] for anger lodges in the lap of fools.
אַל־תְּבַהֵ֥ל בְּרֽוּחֲךָ֖ לִכְע֑וֹס כִּ֣י כַ֔עַס בְּחֵ֥יק כְּסִילִ֖ים יָנֽוּחַ׃
Do not say, "Why were the former days better than these?" For it is not from wisdom that you ask about this.
אַל־תֹּאמַר֙ מֶ֣ה הָיָ֔ה שֶׁ֤הַיָּמִים֙ הָרִ֣אשֹׁנִ֔ים הָי֥וּ טוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֛י לֹ֥א מֵחָכְמָ֖ה שָׁאַ֥לְתָּ עַל־זֶֽה׃
Wisdom is good with an inheritance,[^9] and an advantage to those who see the sun.
טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה עִֽם־נַחֲלָ֑ה וְיֹתֵ֖ר לְרֹאֵ֥י הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
For to be in the shade of wisdom is to be in the shade of money,[^10] and the advantage of knowledge is this: wisdom gives life to those who have it.
כִּ֛י בְּצֵ֥ל הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה בְּצֵ֣ל הַכָּ֑סֶף וְיִתְר֣וֹן דַּ֔עַת הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תְּחַיֶּ֥ה בְעָלֶֽיהָ׃
Consider the work of God: who can make straight what he has made crooked?
רְאֵ֖ה אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּ֣י מִ֤י יוּכַל֙ לְתַקֵּ֔ן אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִוְּתֽוֹ׃
In the day of prosperity, be glad,[^11] and in the day of adversity, consider: God has made the one as well as the other, so that no one can find out anything that will come after him.
בְּי֤וֹם טוֹבָה֙ הֱיֵ֣ה בְט֔וֹב וּבְי֥וֹם רָעָ֖ה רְאֵ֑ה גַּ֣ם אֶת־זֶ֤ה לְעֻמַּת־זֶה֙ עָשָׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים עַל־דִּבְרַ֗ת שֶׁלֹּ֨א יִמְצָ֧א הָֽאָדָ֛ם אַחֲרָ֖יו מְאֽוּמָה׃
In my days of vapor[^12] I have seen everything: there is a righteous person who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked person who lives long in his wickedness.
אֶת־הַכֹּ֥ל רָאִ֖יתִי בִּימֵ֣י הֶבְלִ֑י יֵ֤שׁ צַדִּיק֙ אֹבֵ֣ד בְּצִדְק֔וֹ וְיֵ֣שׁ רָשָׁ֔ע מַאֲרִ֖יךְ בְּרָעָתֽוֹ׃
Do not be too righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why destroy yourself?
אַל־תְּהִ֤י צַדִּיק֙ הַרְבֵּ֔ה וְאַל־תִּתְחַכַּ֖ם יוֹתֵ֑ר לָ֖מָּה תִּשּׁוֹמֵֽם׃
Do not be too wicked, and do not be a fool. Why die before your time?
אַל־תִּרְשַׁ֥ע הַרְבֵּ֖ה וְאַל־תְּהִ֣י סָכָ֑ל לָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּת בְּלֹ֥א עִתֶּֽךָ׃
It is good that you should take hold of the one and not let go of the other,[^13] for whoever fears God will come through with both.[^14]
ט֚וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֶּאֱחֹ֣ז בָּזֶ֔ה וְגַם־מִזֶּ֖ה אַל־תַּנַּ֣ח אֶת־יָדֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי־יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים יֵצֵ֥א אֶת־כֻּלָּֽם׃
Wisdom makes the wise stronger than ten rulers in a city.
הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תָּעֹ֣ז לֶחָכָ֑ם מֵֽעֲשָׂרָה֙ שַׁלִּיטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ בָּעִֽיר׃
Surely there is no one on earth so righteous that he does good and never sins.[^15]
כִּ֣י אָדָ֔ם אֵ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק בָּאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂה־טּ֖וֹב וְלֹ֥א יֶחֱטָֽא׃
Also, do not take to heart all the things that people say, or you may hear your servant[^16] cursing you.
גַּ֤ם לְכָל־הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ אַל־תִּתֵּ֖ן לִבֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־תִשְׁמַ֥ע אֶֽת־עַבְדְּךָ֖ מְקַלְלֶֽךָ׃
For your heart knows that many times you yourself have cursed others.
כִּ֛י גַּם־פְּעָמִ֥ים רַבּ֖וֹת יָדַ֣ע לִבֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר גַּם־*את **אַתָּ֖ה קִלַּ֥לְתָּ אֲחֵרִֽים׃
All this I tested by wisdom. I said, "I will be wise," but it was far from me.
כָּל־זֹ֖ה נִסִּ֣יתִי בַֽחָכְמָ֑ה אָמַ֣רְתִּי אֶחְכָּ֔מָה וְהִ֖יא רְחוֹקָ֥ה מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
What exists is far off, and deep, very deep. Who can find it out?
רָח֖וֹק מַה־שֶּׁהָיָ֑ה וְעָמֹ֥ק ׀ עָמֹ֖ק מִ֥י יִמְצָאֶֽנּוּ׃
I turned, I and my heart, to know and to explore and to seek wisdom and the sum of things,[^17] and to know that wickedness is folly and that foolishness is madness.
סַבּ֨וֹתִֽי אֲנִ֤י וְלִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת וְלָת֔וּר וּבַקֵּ֥שׁ חָכְמָ֖ה וְחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן וְלָדַ֙עַת֙ רֶ֣שַׁע כֶּ֔סֶל וְהַסִּכְל֖וּת הוֹלֵלֽוֹת׃
And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net and whose hands are chains. The one who pleases God[^18] escapes her, but the sinner is caught by her.[^19]
וּמוֹצֶ֨א אֲנִ֜י מַ֣ר מִמָּ֗וֶת אֶת־הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֲשֶׁר־הִ֨יא מְצוֹדִ֧ים וַחֲרָמִ֛ים לִבָּ֖הּ אֲסוּרִ֣ים יָדֶ֑יהָ ט֞וֹב לִפְנֵ֤י הָאֱלֹהִים֙ יִמָּלֵ֣ט מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְחוֹטֵ֖א יִלָּ֥כֶד בָּֽהּ׃
"See, this is what I have found," says the Teacher,[^20] "adding one thing to another to find the sum,
רְאֵה֙ זֶ֣ה מָצָ֔אתִי אָמְרָ֖ה קֹהֶ֑לֶת אַחַ֥ת לְאַחַ֖ת לִמְצֹ֥א חֶשְׁבּֽוֹן׃
which my soul still seeks but I have not found: one man[^21] among a thousand I have found, but a woman among all these I have not found.
אֲשֶׁ֛ר עוֹד־בִּקְשָׁ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֑אתִי אָדָ֞ם אֶחָ֤ד מֵאֶ֙לֶף֙ מָצָ֔אתִי וְאִשָּׁ֥ה בְכָל־אֵ֖לֶּה לֹ֥א מָצָֽאתִי׃
Only see, this I have found: that God made human beings upright, but they have sought out many schemes."[^22]
לְבַד֙ רְאֵה־זֶ֣ה מָצָ֔אתִי אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֧ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הָאָדָ֖ם יָשָׁ֑ר וְהֵ֥מָּה בִקְשׁ֖וּ חִשְּׁבֹנ֥וֹת רַּבִּֽים׃

n.3: Literally "for by sadness of face the heart is made good". Or "the heart is made better".
n.4: A play on words: *sirim*, "thorns", under the *sir*, "pot".
n.7: Literally "better long of spirit than high of spirit".
n.8: The verb is from *ka'as*, translated "grief" in verse 3.
n.9: Or "Wisdom is as good as an inheritance".
n.10: Literally "For in the shade of wisdom, in the shade of silver". Shade is a picture of protection.
n.11: Literally "In the day of good, be in good".
n.12: Literally "in the days of my vapor", that is, in my brief life.
n.13: Literally "and also from this do not rest your hand".
n.14: Literally "will go out with all of them". Or "will avoid all extremes".
n.17: Hebrew *cheshbon*, "reckoning, account, explanation". Also in verse 27.
n.19: Some see here the dangerous woman of Proverbs 5 and 7, or Folly pictured as a woman (Proverbs 9:13–18).

n.22: Hebrew *chishvonot*, a play on *cheshbon*, "sum", in verses 25 and 27.

v: Who is like the wise? And who knows the interpretation of a thing? A person's wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.[^1]
מִ֚י כְּהֶ֣חָכָ֔ם וּמִ֥י יוֹדֵ֖עַ פֵּ֣שֶׁר דָּבָ֑ר חָכְמַ֤ת אָדָם֙ תָּאִ֣יר פָּנָ֔יו וְעֹ֥ז פָּנָ֖יו יְשֻׁנֶּֽא׃
I say:[^2] Keep the king's command,[^3] because of the oath before God.[^4]
אֲנִי֙ פִּי־מֶ֣לֶךְ שְׁמ֔וֹר וְעַ֕ל דִּבְרַ֖ת שְׁבוּעַ֥ת אֱלֹהִֽים׃
Do not be in a hurry to leave his presence. Do not persist in an evil matter, for he does whatever he pleases.
אַל־תִּבָּהֵ֤ל מִפָּנָיו֙ תֵּלֵ֔ךְ אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹ֖ד בְּדָבָ֣ר רָ֑ע כִּ֛י כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַחְפֹּ֖ץ יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃
For the king's word is power, and who can say to him, "What are you doing?"
בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דְּבַר־מֶ֖לֶךְ שִׁלְט֑וֹן וּמִ֥י יֹֽאמַר־ל֖וֹ מַֽה־תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃
Whoever keeps a command will know no harm,[^5] and a wise heart knows the time and the way.[^6]
שׁוֹמֵ֣ר מִצְוָ֔ה לֹ֥א יֵדַ֖ע דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע וְעֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֔ט יֵדַ֖ע לֵ֥ב חָכָֽם׃
For there is a time and a way for every matter, though a person's trouble lies heavy on him.
כִּ֣י לְכָל־חֵ֔פֶץ יֵ֖שׁ עֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּֽי־רָעַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם רַבָּ֥ה עָלָֽיו׃
For he does not know what will happen, and who can tell him how it will happen?
כִּֽי־אֵינֶ֥נּוּ יֹדֵ֖עַ מַה־שֶׁיִּֽהְיֶ֑ה כִּ֚י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִֽהְיֶ֔ה מִ֖י יַגִּ֥יד לֽוֹ׃
No one has power over the wind[^7] to hold back the wind, and no one has power over the day of death. There is no discharge in war, and wickedness will not save those who practice it.[^8]
אֵ֣ין אָדָ֞ם שַׁלִּ֤יט בָּר֙וּחַ֙ לִכְל֣וֹא אֶת־הָר֔וּחַ וְאֵ֤ין שִׁלְטוֹן֙ בְּי֣וֹם הַמָּ֔וֶת וְאֵ֥ין מִשְׁלַ֖חַת בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־יְמַלֵּ֥ט רֶ֖שַׁע אֶת־בְּעָלָֽיו׃
All this I have seen, as I set my heart on every deed that is done under the sun, at a time when one person has power over another to his harm.[^9]
אֶת־כָּל־זֶ֤ה רָאִ֙יתִי֙ וְנָת֣וֹן אֶת־לִבִּ֔י לְכָֽל־מַעֲשֶׂ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עֵ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֧ט הָאָדָ֛ם בְּאָדָ֖ם לְרַ֥ע לֽוֹ׃
And then I saw the wicked buried. They used to come and go from the holy place, and they were forgotten in the city where they had done such things.[^10] This too is vapor.[^11]
וּבְכֵ֡ן רָאִיתִי֩ רְשָׁעִ֨ים קְבֻרִ֜ים וָבָ֗אוּ וּמִמְּק֤וֹם קָדוֹשׁ֙ יְהַלֵּ֔כוּ וְיִֽשְׁתַּכְּח֥וּ בָעִ֖יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר כֵּן־עָשׂ֑וּ גַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃
Because the sentence against an evil deed is not carried out quickly, the hearts of human beings are fully set on doing evil.
אֲשֶׁר֙ אֵין־נַעֲשָׂ֣ה פִתְגָ֔ם מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ה מְהֵרָ֑ה עַל־כֵּ֡ן מָלֵ֞א לֵ֧ב בְּֽנֵי־הָאָדָ֛ם בָּהֶ֖ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת רָֽע׃
Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and lives long,[^12] yet I also know that it will be well with those who fear God, who fear before him.
אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֹטֶ֗א עֹשֶׂ֥ה רָ֛ע מְאַ֖ת וּמַאֲרִ֣יךְ ל֑וֹ כִּ֚י גַּם־יוֹדֵ֣עַ אָ֔נִי אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִהְיֶה־טּוֹב֙ לְיִרְאֵ֣י הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽירְא֖וּ מִלְּפָנָֽיו׃
But it will not be well with the wicked, and he will not lengthen his days like a shadow,[^13] because he does not fear before God.
וְטוֹב֙ לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה לָֽרָשָׁ֔ע וְלֹֽא־יַאֲרִ֥יךְ יָמִ֖ים כַּצֵּ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר אֵינֶ֥נּוּ יָרֵ֖א מִלִּפְנֵ֥י אֱלֹהִֽים׃

There is a vapor that occurs on earth:[^14] there are righteous people who are treated as the deeds of the wicked deserve, and there are wicked people who are treated as the deeds of the righteous deserve. I said that this too is vapor.

יֶשׁ־הֶבֶל֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲשָׂ֣ה עַל־הָאָרֶץ֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר ׀ יֵ֣שׁ צַדִּיקִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר מַגִּ֤יעַ אֲלֵהֶם֙ כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָרְשָׁעִ֔ים וְיֵ֣שׁ רְשָׁעִ֔ים שֶׁמַּגִּ֥יעַ אֲלֵהֶ֖ם כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הַצַדִּיקִ֑ים אָמַ֕רְתִּי שֶׁגַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃

So I commended joy, because there is nothing better for a person under the sun than to eat and drink and be glad. That will go with him in his toil through the days of his life that God has given him under the sun.

וְשִׁבַּ֤חְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ אֶת־הַשִּׂמְחָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֵֽין־ט֤וֹב לָֽאָדָם֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כִּ֛י אִם־לֶאֱכ֥וֹל וְלִשְׁתּ֖וֹת וְלִשְׂמ֑וֹחַ וְה֞וּא יִלְוֶ֣נּוּ בַעֲמָל֗וֹ יְמֵ֥י חַיָּ֛יו אֲשֶׁר־נָֽתַן־ל֥וֹ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
When I set my heart to know wisdom and to see the task that is done on earth (for neither by day nor by night do one's eyes see sleep),
כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤תִּי אֶת־לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת חָכְמָ֔ה וְלִרְאוֹת֙ אֶת־הָ֣עִנְיָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשָׂ֖ה עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֣י גַ֤ם בַּיּוֹם֙ וּבַלַּ֔יְלָה שֵׁנָ֕ה בְּעֵינָ֖יו אֵינֶ֥נּוּ רֹאֶֽה׃

then I saw all the work of God: that no one can find out the work that is done under the sun. However much a person toils to seek it, he will not find it; and even if a wise person claims to know it, he cannot find it out.

וְרָאִיתִי֮ אֶת־כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִים֒ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יוּכַ֜ל הָאָדָ֗ם לִמְצוֹא֙ אֶת־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נַעֲשָׂ֣ה תַֽחַת־הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ בְּ֠שֶׁל אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲמֹ֧ל הָאָדָ֛ם לְבַקֵּ֖שׁ וְלֹ֣א יִמְצָ֑א וְגַ֨ם אִם־יֹאמַ֤ר הֶֽחָכָם֙ לָדַ֔עַת לֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִמְצֹֽא׃

n.1: That is, his stern look is softened.
n.2: Literally "I". The word stands alone in the Hebrew, perhaps meaning "I say", or "I advise you".
n.4: Or "because of your oath to God", or "because of God's oath".
n.5: Literally "will not know an evil thing".
n.6: Literally "time and judgment" (Hebrew *mishpat*): the right time and the right way. Also in verse 6.
n.7: Or "the spirit", the breath of life. Hebrew *ruach*. Also later in the verse.
n.9: Or "to his own harm", or "to the other's harm".
n.10: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "And so I saw the wicked buried, and they came, and from the holy place they go, and they are forgotten in the city where they did so". Some take the second half to mean that those who had acted rightly ("so") and had come from the holy place were forgotten. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the Septuagint read "they were praised" instead of "they were forgotten".
n.13: Or "and his days will not be long; they are like a shadow".
n.14: Literally "There is a vapor that is done on the earth".

v: All this I took to heart, and I sought to make all this clear:[^1] that the righteous and the wise and their deeds are in the hand of God. Whether it is love or hate, no one knows; everything lies before them.[^2]

כִּ֣י אֶת־כָּל־זֶ֞ה נָתַ֤תִּי אֶל־לִבִּי֙ וְלָב֣וּר אֶת־כָּל־זֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הַצַּדִּיקִ֧ים וְהַחֲכָמִ֛ים וַעֲבָדֵיהֶ֖ם בְּיַ֣ד הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים גַּֽם־אַהֲבָ֣ה גַם־שִׂנְאָ֗ה אֵ֤ין יוֹדֵ֙עַ֙ הָֽאָדָ֔ם הַכֹּ֖ל לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

Everything is the same for everyone:[^3] one fate comes to the righteous and the wicked, to the good,[^4] to the clean and the unclean, to the one who offers sacrifices and the one who does not. As it is with the good, so it is with the sinner; as it is with the one who swears an oath, so it is with the one who fears an oath.

הַכֹּ֞ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר לַכֹּ֗ל מִקְרֶ֨ה אֶחָ֜ד לַצַּדִּ֤יק וְלָרָשָׁע֙ לַטּוֹב֙ וְלַטָּה֣וֹר וְלַטָּמֵ֔א וְלַזֹּבֵ֔חַ וְלַאֲשֶׁ֖ר אֵינֶ֣נּוּ זֹבֵ֑חַ כַּטּוֹב֙ כַּֽחֹטֶ֔א הַנִּשְׁבָּ֕ע כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר שְׁבוּעָ֥ה יָרֵֽא׃

This is an evil in all that is done under the sun: that one fate comes to all. The hearts of human beings are full of evil, too, and there is madness in their hearts while they live, and after that they go to the dead.[^5]
זֶ֣ה ׀ רָ֗ע בְּכֹ֤ל אֲשֶֽׁר־נַעֲשָׂה֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כִּֽי־מִקְרֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל וְגַ֣ם לֵ֣ב בְּֽנֵי־הָ֠אָדָם מָלֵא־רָ֨ע וְהוֹלֵל֤וֹת בִּלְבָבָם֙ בְּחַיֵּיהֶ֔ם וְאַחֲרָ֖יו אֶל־הַמֵּתִֽים׃
But whoever is joined[^6] with all the living has hope, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
כִּי־מִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר *יבחר **יְחֻבַּ֔ר אֶ֥ל כָּל־הַחַיִּ֖ים יֵ֣שׁ בִּטָּח֑וֹן כִּֽי־לְכֶ֤לֶב חַי֙ ה֣וּא ט֔וֹב מִן־הָאַרְיֵ֖ה הַמֵּֽת׃
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing at all. They have no more reward, for the memory of them is forgotten.[^7]
כִּ֧י הַֽחַיִּ֛ים יוֹדְעִ֖ים שֶׁיָּמֻ֑תוּ וְהַמֵּתִ֞ים אֵינָ֧ם יוֹדְעִ֣ים מְא֗וּמָה וְאֵֽין־ע֤וֹד לָהֶם֙ שָׂכָ֔ר כִּ֥י נִשְׁכַּ֖ח זִכְרָֽם׃
Their love and their hatred and their envy have already perished, and they will never again have a portion in anything that is done under the sun.
גַּ֣ם אַהֲבָתָ֧ם גַּם־שִׂנְאָתָ֛ם גַּם־קִנְאָתָ֖ם כְּבָ֣ר אָבָ֑דָה וְחֵ֨לֶק אֵין־לָהֶ֥ם עוֹד֙ לְעוֹלָ֔ם בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־נַעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a glad heart, for God has already approved what you do.
לֵ֣ךְ אֱכֹ֤ל בְּשִׂמְחָה֙ לַחְמֶ֔ךָ וּֽשֲׁתֵ֥ה בְלֶב־ט֖וֹב יֵינֶ֑ךָ כִּ֣י כְבָ֔ר רָצָ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶֽת־מַעֲשֶֽׂיךָ׃
Let your clothes always be white, and let your head never lack oil.
בְּכָל־עֵ֕ת יִהְי֥וּ בְגָדֶ֖יךָ לְבָנִ֑ים וְשֶׁ֖מֶן עַל־רֹאשְׁךָ֥ אַל־יֶחְסָֽר׃

Enjoy life[^8] with the wife whom you love, all the days of your life of vapor[^9] that he has given you under the sun, all your days of vapor. For that is your portion in life and in your toil at which you toil under the sun.

רְאֵ֨ה חַיִּ֜ים עִם־אִשָּׁ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־אָהַ֗בְתָּ כָּל־יְמֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י הֶבְלֶ֔ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽתַן־לְךָ֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י הֶבְלֶ֑ךָ כִּ֣י ה֤וּא חֶלְקְךָ֙ בַּֽחַיִּ֔ים וּבַעֲמָ֣לְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your strength, for there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol,[^10] where you are going.
כֹּ֠ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּמְצָ֧א יָֽדְךָ֛ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת בְּכֹחֲךָ֖ עֲשֵׂ֑ה כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה וְחֶשְׁבּוֹן֙ וְדַ֣עַת וְחָכְמָ֔ה בִּשְׁא֕וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה הֹלֵ֥ךְ שָֽׁמָּה׃ ס

Again I saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor riches to the intelligent, nor favor to the skilled, for time and chance happen to them all.

שַׁ֜בְתִּי וְרָאֹ֣ה תַֽחַת־הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֣י לֹא֩ לַקַּלִּ֨ים הַמֵּר֜וֹץ וְלֹ֧א לַגִּבּוֹרִ֣ים הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְ֠גַם לֹ֣א לַחֲכָמִ֥ים לֶ֙חֶם֙ וְגַ֨ם לֹ֤א לַנְּבֹנִים֙ עֹ֔שֶׁר וְגַ֛ם לֹ֥א לַיֹּדְעִ֖ים חֵ֑ן כִּי־עֵ֥ת וָפֶ֖גַע יִקְרֶ֥ה אֶת־כֻּלָּֽם׃
For no one knows his time. Like fish caught in a cruel net, and like birds caught in a snare, so human beings are trapped at an evil time, when it falls on them suddenly.

כִּ֡י גַּם֩ לֹֽא־יֵדַ֨ע הָאָדָ֜ם אֶת־עִתּ֗וֹ כַּדָּגִים֙ שֶׁנֶּֽאֱחָזִים֙ בִּמְצוֹדָ֣ה רָעָ֔ה וְכַ֨צִּפֳּרִ֔ים הָאֲחֻז֖וֹת בַּפָּ֑ח כָּהֵ֗ם יֽוּקָשִׁים֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָֽאָדָ֔ם לְעֵ֣ת רָעָ֔ה כְּשֶׁתִּפּ֥וֹל עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם פִּתְאֹֽם׃
This too I saw as wisdom under the sun, and it seemed great to me.
גַּם־זֹ֛ה רָאִ֥יתִי חָכְמָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ וּגְדוֹלָ֥ה הִ֖יא אֵלָֽי׃
There was a small city with few people in it, and a great king came against it, surrounded it, and built great siegeworks[^11] against it.
עִ֣יר קְטַנָּ֔ה וַאֲנָשִׁ֥ים בָּ֖הּ מְעָ֑ט וּבָֽא־אֵלֶ֜יהָ מֶ֤לֶךְ גָּדוֹל֙ וְסָבַ֣ב אֹתָ֔הּ וּבָנָ֥ה עָלֶ֖יהָ מְצוֹדִ֥ים גְּדֹלִֽים׃
Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.[^12]
וּמָ֣צָא בָ֗הּ אִ֤ישׁ מִסְכֵּן֙ חָכָ֔ם וּמִלַּט־ה֥וּא אֶת־הָעִ֖יר בְּחָכְמָת֑וֹ וְאָדָם֙ לֹ֣א זָכַ֔ר אֶת־הָאִ֥ישׁ הַמִּסְכֵּ֖ן הַהּֽוּא׃
So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength, but the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard."
וְאָמַ֣רְתִּי אָ֔נִי טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה מִגְּבוּרָ֑ה וְחָכְמַ֤ת הַמִּסְכֵּן֙ בְּזוּיָ֔ה וּדְבָרָ֖יו אֵינָ֥ם נִשְׁמָעִֽים׃
The words of the wise, heard in quiet, are better than the shouting of a ruler among fools.
דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֔ים בְּנַ֖חַת נִשְׁמָעִ֑ים מִזַּעֲקַ֥ת מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בַּכְּסִילִֽים׃
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה מִכְּלֵ֣י קְרָ֑ב וְחוֹטֶ֣א אֶחָ֔ד יְאַבֵּ֥ד טוֹבָ֖ה הַרְבֵּֽה׃

n.2: Or "everything that lies before them is vapor". The Septuagint reads this, with "vapor" (Greek *mataiotes*, its word for *hevel*) in place of the first word of verse 2, "everything".
n.4: The Septuagint adds "and to the bad".
n.5: Literally "and after him, to the dead".
n.6: The Hebrew text is written "whoever is chosen" but read "whoever is joined".
n.7: A play on words: *sakhar*, "reward", and *zikhram*, "the memory of them".
n.9: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor"; see 1:2. Here, as in 6:12 and 7:15, the sense is "fleeting".
n.10: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.11: Hebrew *metsodim*, "nets" or "strongholds", here the works built to besiege a city.
n.12: Or "and he could have saved the city by his wisdom, but no one remembered that poor man".

v: Dead flies[^1] make the perfumer's oil stink and ferment; a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.[^2]
זְב֣וּבֵי מָ֔וֶת יַבְאִ֥ישׁ יַבִּ֖יעַ שֶׁ֣מֶן רוֹקֵ֑חַ יָקָ֛ר מֵחָכְמָ֥ה מִכָּב֖וֹד סִכְל֥וּת מְעָֽט׃
The heart of the wise is at his right hand, but the heart of the fool at his left.[^3]
לֵ֤ב חָכָם֙ לִֽימִינ֔וֹ וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִ֖יל לִשְׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃
Even when a fool[^4] walks along the road, he lacks sense,[^5] and he shows everyone that he is a fool.[^6]
וְגַם־בַּדֶּ֛רֶךְ *כשה[y]*סכל **כְּשֶׁסָּכָ֥ל הֹלֵ֖ךְ לִבּ֣וֹ חָסֵ֑ר וְאָמַ֥ר לַכֹּ֖ל סָכָ֥ל הֽוּא׃
If the ruler's anger[^7] rises against you, do not leave your place, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.
אִם־ר֤וּחַ הַמּוֹשֵׁל֙ תַּעֲלֶ֣ה עָלֶ֔יךָ מְקוֹמְךָ֖ אַל־תַּנַּ֑ח כִּ֣י מַרְפֵּ֔א יַנִּ֖יחַ חֲטָאִ֥ים גְּדוֹלִֽים׃
There is an evil I have seen under the sun, like a mistake[^8] that comes from the ruler:
יֵ֣שׁ רָעָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ כִּשְׁגָגָ֕ה שֶׁיֹּצָ֖א מִלִּפְנֵ֥י הַשַּׁלִּֽיט׃
folly is set in many high places, while the rich sit in low places.
נִתַּ֣ן הַסֶּ֔כֶל בַּמְּרוֹמִ֖ים רַבִּ֑ים וַעֲשִׁירִ֖ים בַּשֵּׁ֥פֶל יֵשֵֽׁבוּ׃
I have seen servants[^9] on horses, and princes walking on foot like servants.
רָאִ֥יתִי עֲבָדִ֖ים עַל־סוּסִ֑ים וְשָׂרִ֛ים הֹלְכִ֥ים כַּעֲבָדִ֖ים עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Whoever digs a pit may fall into it, and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
חֹפֵ֥ר גּוּמָּ֖ץ בּ֣וֹ יִפּ֑וֹל וּפֹרֵ֥ץ גָּדֵ֖ר יִשְּׁכֶ֥נּוּ נָחָֽשׁ׃
Whoever quarries stones may be hurt by them, and whoever splits logs may be endangered by them.
מַסִּ֣יעַ אֲבָנִ֔ים יֵעָצֵ֖ב בָּהֶ֑ם בּוֹקֵ֥עַ עֵצִ֖ים יִסָּ֥כֶן בָּֽם׃
If the iron is blunt and one does not sharpen its edge, he must use more strength; but wisdom has the advantage of bringing success.[^10]
אִם־קֵהָ֣ה הַבַּרְזֶ֗ל וְהוּא֙ לֹא־פָנִ֣ים קִלְקַ֔ל וַחֲיָלִ֖ים יְגַבֵּ֑ר וְיִתְר֥וֹן *הכשי[y]*ר **הַכְשֵׁ֖ר חָכְמָֽה׃
If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no gain[^11] for the charmer.[^12]
אִם־יִשֹּׁ֥ךְ הַנָּחָ֖שׁ בְּלוֹא־לָ֑חַשׁ וְאֵ֣ין יִתְר֔וֹן לְבַ֖עַל הַלָּשֽׁוֹן׃
The words of a wise person's mouth win favor,[^13] but the lips of a fool swallow him up.
דִּבְרֵ֥י פִי־חָכָ֖ם חֵ֑ן וְשִׂפְת֥וֹת כְּסִ֖יל תְּבַלְּעֶֽנּוּ׃
The words of his mouth begin in folly, and his talk ends in evil madness.
תְּחִלַּ֥ת דִּבְרֵי־פִ֖יהוּ סִכְל֑וּת וְאַחֲרִ֣ית פִּ֔יהוּ הוֹלֵל֖וּת רָעָֽה׃
The fool multiplies words, though no one knows what will happen; and what will come after him, who can tell him?
וְהַסָּכָ֖ל יַרְבֶּ֣ה דְבָרִ֑ים לֹא־יֵדַ֤ע הָאָדָם֙ מַה־שֶׁיִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִֽהְיֶה֙ מֵֽאַחֲרָ֔יו מִ֖י יַגִּ֥יד לֽוֹ׃
The toil of fools wears them out, for they do not even know the way to the city.[^14]
עֲמַ֥ל הַכְּסִילִ֖ים תְּיַגְּעֶ֑נּוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יָדַ֖ע לָלֶ֥כֶת אֶל־עִֽיר׃
Woe to you, O land, whose king is a youth,[^15] and whose princes feast in the morning!
אִֽי־לָ֣ךְ אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ נָ֑עַר וְשָׂרַ֖יִךְ בַּבֹּ֥קֶר יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃
Happy are you, O land, whose king is the son of nobles, and whose princes eat at the proper time, for strength and not for drunkenness!
אַשְׁרֵ֣יךְ אֶ֔רֶץ שֶׁמַּלְכֵּ֖ךְ בֶּן־חוֹרִ֑ים וְשָׂרַ֙יִךְ֙ בָּעֵ֣ת יֹאכֵ֔לוּ בִּגְבוּרָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א בַשְּׁתִֽי׃
Through laziness the roof sinks in, and through idle hands the house leaks.
בַּעֲצַלְתַּ֖יִם יִמַּ֣ךְ הַמְּקָרֶ֑ה וּבְשִׁפְל֥וּת יָדַ֖יִם יִדְלֹ֥ף הַבָּֽיִת׃
For laughter they make a feast,[^16] and wine gladdens life, and money answers everything.[^17]
לִשְׂחוֹק֙ עֹשִׂ֣ים לֶ֔חֶם וְיַ֖יִן יְשַׂמַּ֣ח חַיִּ֑ים וְהַכֶּ֖סֶף יַעֲנֶ֥ה אֶת־הַכֹּֽל׃
Even in your thoughts do not curse the king, and in your bedroom do not curse the rich, for a bird of the air may carry your voice, and a winged creature may tell the matter.
גַּ֣ם בְּמַדָּֽעֲךָ֗ מֶ֚לֶךְ אַל־תְּקַלֵּ֔ל וּבְחַדְרֵי֙ מִשְׁכָּ֣בְךָ֔ אַל־תְּקַלֵּ֖ל עָשִׁ֑יר כִּ֣י ע֤וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ יוֹלִ֣יךְ אֶת־הַקּ֔וֹל וּבַ֥עַל *הכנפים **כְּנָפַ֖יִם יַגֵּ֥יד דָּבָֽר׃

n.2: Literally "Weightier than wisdom, than honor, is a little folly".
n.3: The right hand stood for strength and favor, the left for misfortune.
n.4: The Hebrew text is written "the fool" but read "a fool".
n.6: Literally "and he says to everyone, he is a fool". Or "and he says of everyone that they are fools".
n.9: Or "slaves". Also later in the verse.
n.10: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Literally "and the advantage of making successful is wisdom".
n.14: Perhaps a saying for someone who cannot do even the simplest thing.
n.15: Or "a servant". Hebrew *na'ar* can mean either, and the contrast in verse 17 is with a king of noble birth.
n.17: Or "money provides for everything", or "money keeps everyone busy".

v: Send your bread out on the surface of the waters, for after many days you will find it.[^1]
שַׁלַּ֥ח לַחְמְךָ֖ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַמָּ֑יִם כִּֽי־בְרֹ֥ב הַיָּמִ֖ים תִּמְצָאֶֽנּוּ׃
Give a portion to seven, and even to eight, for you do not know what disaster may come upon the earth.
תֶּן־חֵ֥לֶק לְשִׁבְעָ֖ה וְגַ֣ם לִשְׁמוֹנָ֑ה כִּ֚י לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע מַה־יִּהְיֶ֥ה רָעָ֖ה עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
If the clouds are full, they pour out rain on the earth; and whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it will lie.
אִם־יִמָּלְא֨וּ הֶעָבִ֥ים גֶּ֙שֶׁם֙ עַל־הָאָ֣רֶץ יָרִ֔יקוּ וְאִם־יִפּ֥וֹל עֵ֛ץ בַּדָּר֖וֹם וְאִ֣ם בַּצָּפ֑וֹן מְק֛וֹם שֶׁיִפּ֥וֹל הָעֵ֖ץ שָׁ֥ם יְהֽוּא׃
Whoever watches the wind will not sow, and whoever looks at the clouds will not reap.
שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע וְרֹאֶ֥ה בֶעָבִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִקְצֽוֹר׃
Just as you do not know the way of the wind,[^2] or how the bones are formed in the womb of a pregnant woman,[^3] so you do not know the work of God, who makes everything.
כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֙עַ֙ מַה־דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָר֔וּחַ כַּעֲצָמִ֖ים בְּבֶ֣טֶן הַמְּלֵאָ֑ה כָּ֗כָה לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙ אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה אֶת־הַכֹּֽל׃
In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not let your hand rest, for you do not know which will succeed, this or that, or whether both alike will be good.
בַּבֹּ֙קֶר֙ זְרַ֣ע אֶת־זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וְלָעֶ֖רֶב אַל־תַּנַּ֣ח יָדֶ֑ךָ כִּי֩ אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע אֵ֣י זֶ֤ה יִכְשָׁר֙ הֲזֶ֣ה אוֹ־זֶ֔ה וְאִם־שְׁנֵיהֶ֥ם כְּאֶחָ֖ד טוֹבִֽים׃
Light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.
וּמָת֖וֹק הָא֑וֹר וְט֥וֹב לַֽעֵינַ֖יִם לִרְא֥וֹת אֶת־הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
For if a person lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. All that comes is vapor.[^4]
כִּ֣י אִם־שָׁנִ֥ים הַרְבֵּ֛ה יִחְיֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם בְּכֻלָּ֣ם יִשְׂמָ֑ח וְיִזְכֹּר֙ אֶת־יְמֵ֣י הַחֹ֔שֶׁךְ כִּֽי־הַרְבֵּ֥ה יִהְי֖וּ כָּל־שֶׁבָּ֥א הָֽבֶל׃

Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes,[^5] but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.

שְׂמַ֧ח בָּח֣וּר בְּיַלְדוּתֶ֗יךָ וִֽיטִּֽ[t]יבְךָ֤ לִבְּךָ֙ בִּימֵ֣י בְחוּרוֹתֶ֔ךָ וְהַלֵּךְ֙ בְּדַרְכֵ֣י לִבְּךָ֔ וּבְמַרְאֵ֖י עֵינֶ֑יךָ וְדָ֕ע כִּ֧י עַל־כָּל־אֵ֛לֶּה יְבִֽיאֲךָ֥ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
Remove grief from your heart, and put away trouble from your body,[^6] for youth and the prime of life[^7] are vapor.
וְהָסֵ֥ר כַּ֙עַס֙ מִלִּבֶּ֔ךָ וְהַעֲבֵ֥ר רָעָ֖ה מִבְּשָׂרֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי־הַיַּלְד֥וּת וְהַֽשַּׁחֲר֖וּת הָֽבֶל׃

n.1: Perhaps a picture of trading by sea, or of generosity that is repaid.
n.2: Or "the way of the breath (or spirit) into the bones in the womb". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.3: Literally "like the bones in the womb of the full one".
n.7: Hebrew *shacharut*, a word found only here: perhaps "the dawn of life" (from *shachar*, "dawn"), or "the time of black hair" (from *shachor*, "black").

v: Remember your Creator[^1] in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and the years draw near when you will say, "I have no pleasure in them";
וּזְכֹר֙ אֶת־בּ֣וֹרְאֶ֔יךָ בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹא־יָבֹ֙אוּ֙ יְמֵ֣י הָֽרָעָ֔ה וְהִגִּ֣יעוּ שָׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאמַ֔ר אֵֽין־לִ֥י בָהֶ֖ם חֵֽפֶץ׃
before the sun and the light, the moon and the stars grow dark, and the clouds return after the rain;
עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־תֶחְשַׁ֤ךְ הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ וְהָא֔וֹר וְהַיָּרֵ֖חַ וְהַכּוֹכָבִ֑ים וְשָׁ֥בוּ הֶעָבִ֖ים אַחַ֥ר הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃
in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, and the strong men are bent, and the women who grind stop because they are few, and those who look through the windows grow dim;[^2]
בַּיּ֗וֹם שֶׁיָּזֻ֙עוּ֙ שֹׁמְרֵ֣י הַבַּ֔יִת וְהִֽתְעַוְּת֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וּבָטְל֤וּ הַטֹּֽחֲנוֹת֙ כִּ֣י מִעֵ֔טוּ וְחָשְׁכ֥וּ הָרֹא֖וֹת בָּאֲרֻבּֽוֹת׃
when the doors to the street are shut, as the sound of the mill grows low, and one rises at the sound of a bird,[^3] and all the daughters of song[^4] are brought low;
וְסֻגְּר֤וּ דְלָתַ֙יִם֙ בַּשּׁ֔וּק בִּשְׁפַ֖ל ק֣וֹל הַֽטַּחֲנָ֑ה וְיָקוּם֙ לְק֣וֹל הַצִּפּ֔וֹר וְיִשַּׁ֖חוּ כָּל־בְּנ֥וֹת הַשִּֽׁיר׃

when people are afraid of what is high, and terrors are on the road; when the almond tree blossoms, and the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caper berry fails;[^5] for a person is going to his eternal home,[^6] and the mourners go about in the street;

גַּ֣ם מִגָּבֹ֤הַּ יִרָ֙אוּ֙ וְחַתְחַתִּ֣ים בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְיָנֵ֤אץ הַשָּׁקֵד֙ וְיִסְתַּבֵּ֣ל הֶֽחָגָ֔ב וְתָפֵ֖ר הָֽאֲבִיּוֹנָ֑ה כִּֽי־הֹלֵ֤ךְ הָאָדָם֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית עוֹלָמ֔וֹ וְסָבְב֥וּ בָשּׁ֖וּק הַסֹּפְדִֽים׃
before the silver cord is snapped[^7] and the golden bowl is broken, and the jar is shattered at the spring, and the wheel is broken at the cistern;[^8]
עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־*ירחק **יֵרָתֵק֙ חֶ֣בֶל הַכֶּ֔סֶף וְתָרֻ֖ץ גֻּלַּ֣ת הַזָּהָ֑ב וְתִשָּׁ֤בֶר כַּד֙ עַל־הַמַּבּ֔וּעַ וְנָרֹ֥ץ הַגַּלְגַּ֖ל אֶל־הַבּֽוֹר׃
and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit[^9] returns to God who gave it.
וְיָשֹׁ֧ב הֶעָפָ֛ר עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּשֶׁהָיָ֑ה וְהָר֣וּחַ תָּשׁ֔וּב אֶל־הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְתָנָֽהּ׃
"Vapor of vapors,"[^10] says the Teacher,[^11] "everything is vapor."
הֲבֵ֧ל הֲבָלִ֛ים אָמַ֥ר הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת הַכֹּ֥ל הָֽבֶל׃
Besides being wise, the Teacher also taught the people knowledge. He weighed,[^12] searched out and arranged many proverbs.
וְיֹתֵ֕ר שֶׁהָיָ֥ה קֹהֶ֖לֶת חָכָ֑ם ע֗וֹד לִמַּד־דַּ֙עַת֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְאִזֵּ֣ן וְחִקֵּ֔ר תִּקֵּ֖ן מְשָׁלִ֥ים הַרְבֵּֽה׃
The Teacher sought to find pleasing words, and to write words of truth correctly.[^13]
בִּקֵּ֣שׁ קֹהֶ֔לֶת לִמְצֹ֖א דִּבְרֵי־חֵ֑פֶץ וְכָת֥וּב יֹ֖שֶׁר דִּבְרֵ֥י אֱמֶֽת׃
The words of the wise are like goads, and like nails firmly fixed are the collected sayings;[^14] they are given by one shepherd.[^15]
דִּבְרֵ֤י חֲכָמִים֙ כַּדָּ֣רְבֹנ֔וֹת וּֽכְמַשְׂמְר֥וֹת נְטוּעִ֖ים בַּעֲלֵ֣י אֲסֻפּ֑וֹת נִתְּנ֖וּ מֵרֹעֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃
Beyond these, my son, be warned. Of making many books there is no end, and much study wearies the body.[^16]
וְיֹתֵ֥ר מֵהֵ֖מָּה בְּנִ֣י הִזָּהֵ֑ר עֲשׂ֨וֹת סְפָרִ֤ים הַרְבֵּה֙ אֵ֣ין קֵ֔ץ וְלַ֥הַג הַרְבֵּ֖ה יְגִעַ֥ת בָּשָֽׂר׃
The end of the matter; all has been heard. Fear God and keep his commands, for this is the whole of a human being.[^17]
ס֥וֹף דָּבָ֖ר הַכֹּ֣ל נִשְׁמָ֑ע אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים יְרָא֙ וְאֶת־מִצְוֺתָ֣יו שְׁמ֔וֹר כִּי־זֶ֖ה כָּל־הָאָדָֽם׃
For God will bring every deed into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
כִּ֚[t]י אֶת־כָּל־מַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים יָבִ֥א בְמִשְׁפָּ֖ט עַ֣ל כָּל־נֶעְלָ֑ם אִם־ט֖וֹב וְאִם־רָֽע׃

n.1: Hebrew *bor'ekha*, "your Creator", written in a plural form, like the plural of majesty in *Elohim*. Some hear a play on *bor*, "cistern" (compare Proverbs 5:15 and verse 6) or "pit, grave".
n.2: Verses 2–6 picture old age and death. Many take the images as the failing body (the keepers as arms, the women who grind as teeth, those at the windows as eyes); others as a great house or a town falling into silence and decay.
n.3: Or "and the sound of the bird rises".
n.4: That is, the singing voices, or the notes of song.
n.5: Hebrew *aviyyonah*, "caper berry", which was eaten to stir the appetite. The sense is probably that desire fails.
n.7: The Hebrew text is written "is removed" but read "is snapped".
n.8: Hebrew *bor*, perhaps echoing "your Creator" (*bor'ekha*) in verse 1.
n.10: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor": the book ends its words as it began them (1:2).
n.11: Hebrew *ha-qohelet*, "the Teacher", here with the article; see 1:1. Verses 9–14 speak about the Teacher, perhaps in the voice of the one who collected his words.
n.13: Or "and what was written was upright, words of truth".
n.14: Literally "the masters of collections": the collected sayings, or those who collect them. Or "the masters of assemblies".
n.15: The shepherd may be God, or the teacher who gathered the sayings.
n.17: Literally "for this is all the human being". That is, this is the whole duty of everyone, or this is what every person is for.
